Stage.tsx keys its one motion.div by step.groupKey ?? step.id, so adjacent steps keep the same mounted scene and only the payload prop changes. A single shared groupKey is correct for one continuously evolving scene. Identity: entities.ts owns entityId(name) and a fixed name per entity. sceneStates is cumulative (additions.slice(0, i+1).flat()), so an entity keeps the same name across steps. StoryScene passes identity={entityId(entity.name)} to a kit primitive, and Box, Label, Arrow, Frame and SymbolChip all delegate to Node. dispute_checks{"demo-integration":[],"scene-kit":[],"presentation-skill":[],"verification-tooling":[],"engineering-quality":[{"id":"engineering-presentation-css-scoped","classification":"contradicted","rationale":"The requirement says every selector in a presentation-owned stylesheet must be scoped under the presentation&#39;s own root class or hook, or come from a CSS module. It also says to fail on any unscoped rule. presentation.css is a plain imported stylesheet, not a CSS module. It has many top-level rules that are not nested under the root class `.story`, such as `.story-entity`, `.story-entity small`, `.story-person, .story-skill`, `.story-card` and `.story-reveal`. A shared `story-` prefix in the class name does not place a selector under the `.story` root. The &#39;or hook&#39; wording offers a root hook (for example a root data attribute) as an alternative to the root class. It is not an exemption for any class the presentation names after itself. The auditor narrows the requirement to rules that restyle kit or shared hooks, but the text covers &#39;every selector&#39;; kit-hook selectors are named only as something included (&#39;including&#39;), not as the whole scope. Nothing in the packet shows that these classes cannot be loaded globally. Since the stylesheet is not a CSS module, these unscoped global rules break the requirement as written, and the fail verdict stands.","evidence":["Talk.tsx imports &#39;./presentation.css&#39; as a plain global stylesheet (not a CSS module) and passes className=&quot;story&quot; as the root.","presentation.css has top-level rules not nested under .story: `.story-entity { ... }`, `.story-entity small { ... }`, `.story-person, .story-skill { ... }`, `.story-card { ... }`, `.story-reveal { ..…","The requirement says &#39;every selector ... is scoped under that presentation&#39;s own root class or hook, or comes from a CSS module&#39; and to &#39;Fail when a presentation-owned stylesheet cont…","StoryScene.tsx applies `story-entity story-${entity.kind}`.
